newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Taleban say they reach eastern Kabul outskirts.
newsitem.headline: Taleban say they reach eastern Kabul outskirts.

text.p: The rebel Afghan Taleban militia said its fighters had reached the eastern outskirts of Kabul on Wednesday and were battling government forces there.
Taleban sources quoted by the Pakistan-based Afghan Islamic Press said the rebels had captured Pul-i-Charki village on the eastern outskirts of the capital and the military academy.
They were fighting for control of the customs house area, only five km (three miles) from the city itself, they said.
Government jets were bombing the Taleban, who were attacking Kabul from the east, south and southwest, the sources said.
The Islamic rebels made a lightning thrust up the main Jalalabad-Kabul highway after capturing the key town of Sarobi, 70 km (44 miles) from Kabul, overnight.
